title: Mussolini, Jan. 3, 1925
topic: Mussolini's January 3, 1925 speech to the Chamber of Deputies: the declaration of sole responsibility (translated from Italian, with archival photographs)
caption_extra: The key passage of Mussolini's January 3, 1925 speech to Italy's Chamber of Deputies, months after fascist squads murdered the opposition deputy Giacomo Matteotti. Translated from the Italian text (Wikisource); read by a synthetic English voice, not Mussolini's. Archival photos are public domain via Wikimedia Commons and are from other occasions, not this speech.

beats.narration: I declare here, before this assembly and before the whole Italian people, that I alone assume the political, moral, and historical responsibility for everything that has happened.
beats.label: Italian Chamber of Deputies

beats.narration: If distorted phrases are enough to hang a man, then bring out the pole, and bring out the rope!
beats.label: Mussolini with officials, 1928

beats.narration: If Fascism has been nothing but castor oil and the club, and not instead a proud passion of Italy's best youth, then the blame is mine!
beats.label: Mussolini, 1932 (other occasion)

beats.narration: If Fascism was a criminal association, if all the violence was the result of a certain historical, political, and moral climate, then the responsibility for that is mine, because I created that climate, with a propaganda that runs from Italy's entry into the war until today.
beats.label: Rally crowd, 1926 (other occasion)
